raw_response:
I have been farming these 232.9 mu in Qianhedao for 25 years. My household is only three people, so I hire machines for tillage and harvest, and I bring in workers for cauliflower transplanting and picking because 132.9 mu of vegetables is too much for family labor alone. I split the land into two blocks: 100 mu does wheat then summer maize, and the other 132.9 mu does wheat then autumn cauliflower. I learned this from other family farms nearby — cauliflower gives cash income, but wheat stabilizes the soil and provides grain I can sell.

For wheat, I rotary till before sowing in late October and broadcast 40 jin of improved seed per mu — that is 20 kg — because a thick stand helps me hit 850 jin per mu even if some patches are thin. I spread one bag, 100 jin, of 15-20-10 compound fertilizer as base, then topdress 30 jin of urea when the wheat greens up in spring. That works out to about 14 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice from my well: once before winter to protect the seedlings, and once at jointing. I spray three times total — herbicide at sowing, then insecticide and fungicide later when aphids and rust show up. I would rather spend the money than risk a bad harvest.

For summer maize, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed right after wheat harvest around June 5. I do not till; I direct-seed with the no-till machine to save diesel and time, and the neighbors get the same yield this way. I put down 80 jin per mu of 28-6-6 compound at sowing, which is about 11 kg nitrogen, 2 kg phosphorus, and 2 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice in summer if the rainfall is short, usually when the plants are knee-high and at filling. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide with sowing, and one insecticide if armyworms appear. Last year this gave me 1,100 jin per mu, so I will do the same.

For autumn cauliflower, I transplant Dian hybrid seedlings around early August after the wheat comes off. I rotary plough first because cauliflower needs soft soil for the head to grow big. Base fertilizer is 100 jin per mu of 15-5-20 compound, and I topdress with 75 jin of 22-9-9 when the heads start wrapping. That is about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 13 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate four times — cauliflower drinks heavily — and spray five times: herbicide before transplanting, then insecticide and fungicide alternating because caterpillars and mildew can ruin the whole crop. I expect 3,000 jin per mu if the market holds.

I do not change much from last year. Fertilizer is expensive, but cutting back is false economy — a yield drop costs more than the bag of urea. My budget is tight with hired labor and diesel, but I know these rates work on my land.
